title: A standardized protocol for microplastic and non-synthetic microfiber extraction and µFTIR identification in elasmobranch gastrointestinal tissues☆
author: Cruz-García, Amezcua

steps.title: Gather materials and equipment
steps.instruction: Collect all required items: metal dissection tray, mosquito forceps, scalpel, dissection scissors; 500 mL glass jars with metal lids; 60 × 15 mm glass Petri dishes; 5 mL pipette; vacuum pump and 500 mL vacuum filtration apparatus; Whatman™ GF/C glass‑fiber filters (1.2 µm mesh, 47 mm diameter); 20 % KOH solution; 30 % H₂O₂ solution; 5 M NaCl solution; stereoscopic microscope with Zeiss AxioCam ERC 5s camera; µ‑FTIR‑ATR Nicolet™ iN™10 system with diamond crystal and liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled detector.

steps.title: Prepare clean workspace and PPE
steps.instruction: Work inside a laminar‑flow hood; wear non‑shedding cotton lab coats and nitrile gloves; avoid synthetic clothing; clean dissection area with filtered water; keep all samples covered when not actively processing.

steps.title: Pre‑treat glassware, metal tools, and filters
steps.instruction: Place all glassware, metal instruments, and GF/C filters in an oven at 400 °C for 4 h. Afterwards wash dissection equipment with methanol followed by distilled water that has been pre‑filtered through GF/C filters (1.2 µm) to remove any particles.

steps.title: Extract gastrointestinal tract and store if needed
steps.instruction: Immediately after specimen collection, dissect out the gastrointestinal (GI) tract under the clean hood. If digestion cannot start right away, transfer the GI tract to pre‑cleaned glass containers and freeze at –20 °C.

steps.title: Chemical digestion of tissue
steps.instruction: Place each GI tract piece into a 500 mL glass jar with a metal lid. Add enough 20 % KOH solution and 30 % H₂O₂ solution to fully submerge the tissue. Incubate at ambient temperature for 24–72 h, checking periodically until the tissue is completely dissolved.

substeps.instruction: Seal jar and place on a rocker or shaker (optional).
Monitor digestion; continue until no visible tissue remains (24–72 h).

steps.title: Density separation of microplastics
steps.instruction: After digestion, add 5 M NaCl solution to the jar to create a high‑density medium; gently invert to mix and allow particles to separate by buoyancy.

substeps.instruction: Add sufficient 5 M NaCl to achieve a density >1.2 g cm⁻³.
Mix gently and let the suspension stand for a few minutes.

steps.title: Vacuum filtration of supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant to the 500 mL vacuum filtration apparatus and filter onto a GF/C filter (1.2 µm, 47 mm). Rinse the filtration apparatus with ethanol followed by filtered distilled water between samples. Keep the filtration area covered to avoid airborne deposition.

substeps.instruction: Assemble filtration set‑up with GF/C filter.
Apply vacuum and filter the supernatant.
Rinse filter holder with ethanol, then with filtered distilled water.
Cover the apparatus during and after filtration.

steps.title: Microscopic examination and particle isolation
steps.instruction: Allow the filter to dry, then examine it under a stereomicroscope (10–40×) equipped with a digital camera. Count and photograph all particles ≥150 µm, and manually pick each particle for spectroscopic analysis.

steps.title: Acquire µFTIR‑ATR spectra
steps.instruction: Place each isolated particle on the ATR crystal of the µ‑FTIR‑ATR system. Acquire mid‑infrared spectra using the Nicolet™ iN™10 instrument with the diamond crystal and liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled detector.

steps.title: Identify polymers by spectral matching
steps.instruction: Compare each spectrum against the instrument’s integrated FTIR reference library. Accept a polymer identification when the similarity score is ≥75 %; flag any ambiguous spectra for re‑analysis.

description: The following protocol was developed to extract and identify MPs and other non-synthetic microfibers (NSMs) from elasmobranch gastrointestinal (GI) tissues efficiently. Given the complexity and high organic content of these samples, this protocol prioritizes complete digestion of the tissue, control of background contamination, and recovery of particles without chemical alteration. The workflow is divided into four main stages: sample preparation, chemical digestion, density separation and filtration, and spectroscopic identification. Validation addressed four parameters: recovery efficiency, reproducibility across replicates, polymer integrity after chemical treatment, and the detection limit of each analytical step. Eight tissue samples and one procedural blank (double-distilled water only) were processed under the full protocol. Each was spiked with 100 polyethylene reference microplastics in the 50–500 µm size range before digestion, so that recovery could be measured against a known input. Recovered PE was counted by stereomicroscopy and confirmed by µFTIR-ATR. Recovery was calculated as:Recovery(%)=NumberofMPsRecoveredNumberofMPsIntroduced×100 Across the eight tissue samples, recovery ranged from 90% to 96%, with a mean of 93.4 ± 2.06% (Table 2). The procedural blank returned 97%.
